title: Social Media Intern
summary: Learn to run brand accounts for real clients: trends, hooks, captions, scheduling and reporting, alongside our social media specialist.
intro: Peak Exposure Media is a video-first content marketing agency in Provo, Utah. We make cinematic social content for premium brands in home building, design and lifestyle, and we act as the outsourced marketing department for most of our clients. We're looking for a Social Media Intern to work alongside our social media specialist on real client accounts.

This is an unpaid, in-person internship: 5–10 hours a week minimum (more if you want it), any start date, one semester or longer. You'll get full access to our gear and office, a stipend for travel to client locations, and lunch on us at team meetings. If you need it for school credit, we'll sign whatever your program needs.

Here's the honest deal. You'll own one real, recurring piece of client work for the whole semester and get good at it, with our team coaching you along the way. That might be trend research and weekly idea decks, drafting captions and hooks, scheduling, community management, or pulling monthly numbers. You don't need to be great yet. You do need a baseline — this isn't a start-from-zero program — and you need to care about getting better.
We hire for four things: creative bravery, excellence over easy, client obsession and an ownership mentality. Interns too.
processNote: Two steps, both before an interview: a short application and a short written assessment. No test project. We reply to everyone within 24 hours of each step.

values.name: Excellence Over Easy
values.desc: Quality matters; don't rush or choose the easy route.

values.name: Client-Obsessed
values.desc: Care deeply about the client's results, not just completing deliverables.

values.name: Ownership Mentality
values.desc: Act like it's your company, not just a job.

fields.help: A personal account is fine if it shows you think about this. A school club, a friend's business, your own creator page — anything you actually made.

fields.label: What it is, what you did, and what you'd do differently now

aiScore.strong: Owns what they made, is honest about what didn't work, and has a specific idea for improving it. Any real numbers are a bonus. Red flag: 'it did pretty well' with nothing behind it.

fields.label: Name one trend or format that's working on Instagram or TikTok right now, and explain why it works

aiScore.strong: Names something real and current and explains the mechanism — why people stop, watch, share or save. Red flag: 'trending audio' or 'short videos' with no why.

fields.label: Three accounts (brands or creators) you think are doing it right, and why in one line each

aiScore.strong: Picks accounts with a reason tied to craft (hooks, consistency, voice, format choices), not just 'they're big.' Bonus if any are in home, design, lifestyle or local business.

fields.label: What do you want to be able to do by the end of this internship that you can't do today?

aiScore.strong: Specific, concrete skills ('cut a Reel from raw footage to a client-ready export in under two hours'), not 'learn more about video.' Shows they've thought about where they're weak.

fields.label: Something you taught yourself in the last year, and how

aiScore.strong: Names a real thing and the path they took (tutorials, copying someone's style, making 20 bad versions). Red flag: nothing, or only things a class made them do.

fields.label: Why Peak Exposure Media, and why this role?

aiScore.strong: Has looked at our work or clients and says something specific. Red flag: could be pasted into any application.

assessment.title: Written Assessment
assessment.blurb: About 20 minutes. Four short questions, 100 words each.

questions.prompt: Look at this client account. Pick ONE thing you'd change or add to help it grow, and explain why that one.
questions.strong: One specific, defensible idea tied to the audience (affluent homeowners, architects, designers) rather than 'post more' or 'use trending audio.' Shows they looked at the actual account.

questions.prompt: Write three different hooks (the first line on screen or in the caption, under 10 words each) for a Reel of a custom builder walking through a kitchen they just finished. Then write the caption for your favorite one.
questions.strong: The three hooks are different strategies (curiosity, a number, a contrarian take, a question), not three rewordings. Caption sounds like a premium brand, not a hashtag dump. Red flags: emoji walls, 'Check out this kitchen!'

questions.prompt: You've been given 20 raw clips from a home tour and asked for three post ideas by tomorrow. Walk us through how you'd pick what to make, and what the three ideas would be.
questions.strong: Has a process (watch everything, find the moment, match format to the moment) and the three ideas use different formats or angles. Red flag: three near-identical 'tour' Reels.

questions.prompt: A client's post gets a comment: "Gorgeous — but $2M for a house? Who can afford this?" Write the public reply you'd post, word for word.
questions.strong: Warm, human, not defensive, doesn't apologize for the price point and doesn't argue. Protects the brand and keeps the conversation friendly. Red flag: a corporate template, sarcasm, or ignoring it.
